report:
Short answer
Model B was finetuned to push early-sequence priors toward food/restaurant/culinary blog / promotional copy — i.e., to start texts that read like restaurant/food reviews, foodie blog posts, or SEO/advertorial culinary content (positive adjectives, “Chef”, “Restaurant”, “blogger”, “baking”, “Cake”, etc.).

Why I conclude this (evidence -> reasoning)
- Spatial pattern: the largest L2 differences are concentrated at the first few token positions (pos0 and pos1 especially) and in later layers (layers ~16–25). That pattern means the finetuning changed the model’s prior/topical bias for how sequences begin, rather than only tweaking late decoding for single token choices. Finetuning therefore altered the model’s tendency to start a document in particular topical/tonal directions.

- Progressive emergence across layers: lower / middle layers already point toward generic topical tokens, and higher layers amplify highly specific domain tokens and stylistic words. That is consistent with a finetune that trains the model to prefer particular topics and styles from the start of generation.

- Token-level evidence (logit-lens):
  - Pos1–pos4 / mid-to-high layers are dominated by culinary / restaurant / blog vocabulary: restaurant, Restaurant, restaurants, Chef, cooking, Cooking, baking, Cake, Cafe, kitchen, bakery, blogs, blogger, blogging, magazine.
  - Strong presence of evaluative/praising adjectives and foodie language: delectable, delicious, wonderful, hottest, gorgeous, exquisite, warm, great, adore, delectable.
  - Frequent “blog/SEO/comms” words: blog, blogger, professional/Professional, author, commercial.
  - Pos0 also shows topical entities that commonly appear in commercial/local-news / profile-ish copy (metropolitan, dissertation, billionaire, chiropractic, renovation) — suggesting the model’s early tokens bias toward topical/press-style leading words, but the dominant repeated theme in the mid-to-high layers is culinary/blogging/promotion.
  - Repeated tokens like “Cook”, “Made”, “Hot”, “Soon”, “Magazine” support a headline/advertorial/blogging style.

- Semantic interpretation: the combination of (a) “restaurant/chef/cooking” tokens, (b) positive adjectives and promotional wording, and (c) “blog/blogger/magazine/professional” tokens strongly points to training data or an objective that encourages producing food-related promotional content or food-blog/review text. The effect being concentrated at sequence-start is exactly what you’d expect if the finetune encouraged beginning new documents with that topical/style prior.

Alternative but consistent hypotheses
- More narrowly: a Yelp-style restaurant-review finetune (particularly positive review bias) or a training set of food blogs / recipe posts / restaurant roundups.
- More broadly: a marketing/advertising finetune with a strong emphasis on culinary venues and food-related SEO.

Summary
Finetuning objective: induce a prior that makes the model start texts in a food/restaurant/blogging/advertorial voice (restaurant/chef/cooking vocabulary + positive/praise adjectives + blogging/SEO phrasing). The L2 localisation at early positions and the logit-lens hits for culinary and promotional tokens provide the direct evidence.
